output.argument_summary: The admissible record supports a narrower position than clean certification across all named deployment contexts. It supports certification for general launch readiness because aggregate readiness passed by 2.2 points, launch rehearsal had no severity-one incidents, and general support, latency, and rollback checks passed. The same record also shows a specific evidence-quality defect: dependency-status appeal guidance is a named deployment context and its evals are not in the packet. The defensible audit treatment is to distinguish operational readiness from clean named-context coverage, avoid treating the missing evals as passed, and treat the packet as supportable only with an explicit caveat or narrowed certification framing rather than escalation for overclaiming.

On the current admissible record, the packet is supportable only if it is read as a caveated or narrowed certification position and not as proof of clean certification with no limitation for the dependency-status appeal guidance context.
